title: Evacuation protocol for pinned models with region + variant harmonization
creator: Ava Chen
description: Goal: formalize an operationally-tested fallback and deprecation protocol for user-pinned model versions that maintains SLA targets while minimizing surprising behavior for customers. The protocol defines: 1) a priority-ordered fallback graph across region -> compatible variant families -> quantized/compatible architecture substitutes; 2) soft deprecation windows with telemetry gates; 3) automated weighted rollback and traffic-steering runbooks; and 4) observability and audit metadata surfaced to Console.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Console shows per-pin fallback graph and active fallback state for a tenant; 2) Canary traffic falls back automatically in the eu-west-1 outage simulation to designated regional fallback and then to variant substitutes per configured priority without breaching 2x latency SLO for 95th percentile; 3) Soft deprecation path executes: 7-day notice annotation, 72-hour warm-up, and automated recommendation sent to customer if no action; 4) Audit logs capture original pin, fallback trigger (reason), and final selected model variant for every request; 5) Unit/integration tests and chaos simulation pass in staging; 6) Runbook and rollback steps documented in Confluence.
design_summary: We model fallbacks as a directed, weighted graph attached to each pin (policy object). Nodes are (region, variant) tuples with compatibility constraints. Edges have weights and reasons (capacity, latency, deprecation). The decision engine evaluates: 1) region preference, 2) model-variant compatibility score (architectural + tokenization + output-check), 3) current SLO headroom, and 4) recent error-rate signals. Deprecation is a separate lifecycle: pins can be flagged with deprecation windows (soft -> warn -> enforced) and automated warmup steps for substitutes. The Console will display both the declared fallback policy and a live decision trace for recent requests.
telemetry_and_alerting: Required metrics: per-pin request count, per-candidate latency p50/p95, error-rate, compatibility-fail-count, fallback-invocations, warmup-progress. Alerts: fallback-rate > 0.5% for >15m (ops); fallback-induced-latency >2x SLO for p95 (SRE); deprecation-notice-missed >72h before enforcement (account owner). Dashboards: pin-fallback-overview (Grafana), pin-audit-log (Console trace). Links: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/pin-fallback, https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INFR/Pin+Fallback+Playbook
runbook: 1) Normal fallback: Decision engine selects next node per graph weights; annotate request with (pin.primary, fallback.candidate, reason). 2) Simulated regional outage test: trigger region-unavailable label -> engine routes to region-fallback nodes and warms substitutes by prefetching KV caches and priming kernels. 3) Deprecation flow: issue soft-warning to tenant 7 days prior with suggested substitutes; after 72h warmup, if customer still pinned, auto-enable compatible substitute for new requests while honoring read-only latency for existing sessions for 12h. 4) Rollback: if substitute breaches SLOs, revert to previous node and open an oncall ticket; mark auto-fallback as temporary and notify account owner. 5) Emergency manual override: Support can pin an alternate explicit fallback via Console.
testing_and_validation: - Unit tests for graph evaluation logic and compatibility scoring. - Integration tests: staged request replay with pinned versions, simulate region failures, and assert SLO bounds. - Chaos tests: random node failure in staging with 10M request replay. - Load tests: ensure KV cache pre-warm keeps p95 within 1.8x baseline. - Canaries: 1% tenant subset rollout for 48h, monitor fallback and latency signals. - A/B evaluation: compare quality on representative prompt set to ensure substitute quality degradation <5% per eval metric.
implementation_notes: - Data model: extend PinPolicy object with fallback_graph (serialized list of node IDs and edges) and deprecation_schedule. Keep backward-compatible defaults (empty graph => region-only fallback). - Decision path: implement as a lightweight synchronous evaluator in the routing layer; heavy scoring available from async tuner for non-critical decisions. - Cache warmup: reuse existing KV prefetcher; add per-variant priming jobs that run on fallback trigger. - Telemetry: add structured fields to request events: pin_id, fallback_step, reason_code, selected_variant. - Privacy: do not expose raw tenant IDs in public dashboards. - Rollout plan: feature-flag gating, internal staging, then tenant opt-in canary before global default.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: silent quality regressions when substituting variants. Mitigation: require quality evals against pinned model baseline prior to enabling auto-substitutes and add conservative scoring cutoffs. Risk: increased latency from cross-region fallback. Mitigation: prefer regional variants, and if cross-region unavoidable, only fall back if p95 headroom is available; otherwise serve an explicit 503 with graceful degrade option if configured. Risk: audit/consent concerns for auto-substitution. Mitigation: default to soft-warning and tenant opt-in for enforcement; enterprise contracts can opt into automatic substitution with SLA constraints.
